svg.text: Cost engineering — the part that makes consumer AI shippable
1 · Template-first generation
the deterministic template IS the product — the LLM may
only re-warm the same fact; no key → template still ships
2 · One generation per day, cached
daily brief generates once per calendar day —
reopening the app 20× costs zero
3 · Stable / volatile prompt split
byte-stable prefix (persona, rules, tools) + volatile tail
(today's data) — explicit cache breakpoints, both vendors
4 · Sliding window + memory folding
old chat turns folded into compact notes by the CHEAP
model, off the user's turn — context bounded forever
5 · Bounded outputs + observability
tight max_tokens per feature (300–2,200); every call logs
in / out / cacheRead / cacheWrite to on-device diagnostics
Measured, not vibes
Usage logs caught OpenAI's implicit caching
returning "cached 0" on every 6.5k-token coach
turn. Fix: route gpt-5.6 to the Responses API
with an explicit prompt_cache_breakpoint.
Result on a real key:
82% cached
5,512 of 6,747 input tokens at the 90% discount
cost of one coach turn, before → after
Source: on-device token diagnostics against a live
production key — the same observability that found
the bug. AI polish costs ≤1 cheap-model call per
surface per day; degrades gracefully with no key.
Cache → route → compress → bound — the standard cost ladder, actually implemented end to end,
with the receipts logged on the phone itself
